composition.story: RFE ranks features by the model's weights, but those weights depend on which features are present. Features x1 and x2 are near-duplicates that split one strong signal. Step through the rounds: after x2 is dropped, the refit gives its share back to x1. Switch to "Rank once" to see stale weights discard that signal and lower held-out R².

aha.observation: Once x2 is dropped, the refit moves x1 from 0.36 to 0.70. The rankings changed, so x1 is kept and x4 becomes the weakest.

controls.label: Reset to first step and RFE mode

states.label: Start
states.sentence: There are four features. x1 and x2 are near-duplicates with r = 0.95. The goal is to keep k = 2.
states.why: Assumptions: synthetic data, standardized inputs, one feature dropped per round.

states.label: Fit 1
states.sentence: Fit 1 splits the shared signal between x1 and x2. Weights: x1 0.36, x2 0.34, x3 0.40, x4 0.38.
states.why: Correlated features divide the weight of one signal between them.

states.label: Drop x2
states.sentence: x2 has the smallest weight (0.34), so RFE drops it.
states.why: Each round removes the lowest-ranked feature from the latest fit.

states.label: Refit 2
states.sentence: After the refit, x1 takes back x2's share and rises from 0.36 to 0.70. Now x4 is the weakest.
states.why: A feature's weight depends on which other features are in the model.

states.label: Drop x4
states.sentence: x4 now has the smallest weight (0.38), so RFE drops it.
states.why: This ranking comes from the refit, not from the stale first fit.

states.label: Fit 3 · stop
states.sentence: Fit 3 uses x1 and x3, with weights 0.70 and 0.40. Held-out R² is 0.79. RFE stops at k = 2.
states.why: The strong signal survives because each ranking used the current feature set.

regions.label: Linear model (standardized inputs)
values: k = 2 kept, ranking fixed after fit 1

states.label: Start
states.sentence: There are four features. x1 and x2 are near-duplicates with r = 0.95. The goal is to keep k = 2.
states.why: Same synthetic data, but this mode ranks the features only once.

states.label: Fit 1
states.sentence: Fit 1 splits the shared signal between x1 and x2. Weights: x1 0.36, x2 0.34, x3 0.40, x4 0.38.
states.why: This one ranking will decide every later drop.

states.label: Drop x2
states.sentence: x2 has the smallest weight (0.34), so it is dropped.

states.label: Drop x1
states.sentence: With no refit, the stale ranking still lists x1 at 0.36. That makes x1 the next weakest, so it is dropped.
states.why: x1 never gets back x2's share, so its true strength stays hidden.

states.label: Kept x3, x4
states.sentence: The kept features are x3 and x4. Both copies of the strong shared signal are gone.
states.why: Both duplicate features looked weak only because they shared credit.

states.label: Final fit
states.sentence: The final fit uses x3 and x4. Held-out R² is 0.42, compared with 0.79 when RFE refits.
states.why: Skipping one refit saved compute, but cost most of the predictive signal.
